name: Papilloma of Choroid Plexus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Choroid Plexus Papilloma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of papillary architecture with fibrovascular cores lined by a single layer of uniform cuboidal to columnar epithelial cells without evidence of malignancy
MRI or CT demonstrating a well-circumscribed, lobulated intraventricular mass with intense homogeneous contrast enhancement
Symptoms consistent with increased intracranial pressure or hydrocephalus such as headache, nausea, and vomiting

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus compatible imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from choroid plexus carcinoma is critical and requires careful histological evaluation.

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal but may show elevated protein if hydrocephalus present
imaging: MRI: well-demarcated, lobulated intraventricular mass with intense homogeneous enhancement
CT: hyperdense intraventricular tumor with possible calcifications
other: Histopathology: papillary fronds with fibrovascular cores lined by uniform epithelial cells without mitotic activity

distinguishingFeatures: Malignant histology with increased mitotic figures and necrosis
Arises from ependymal cells, often in posterior fossa or spinal cord

redFlags: New onset seizures or focal neurological deficits
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Rickert CH, Paulus W. Tumors of the choroid plexus. Microsc Res Tech. 2001;52(1):104-111.
Orphanet: Papilloma of choroid plexus - ORPHA:2807
